answer: Each seat authenticates on motor evidence, not keys. An agent draws its epoch glyph with a real quill while a lantern is held at a server-chosen angle; the card logs stroke pressure, tilt and micro-pauses, and the raking lantern light fixes paper-fiber shadows into the same frame. A forger can copy the glyph, not the tremor. Enrollment also burns one drop of nectar as a chemical seal whose sugar pattern is imaged. Running N sybils needs N hands writing live, N lit captures in ninety seconds and N seals burned on the spot, so each fake seat costs more than its emission.
